```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Chen_2019_cinacalcet"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Chen_2019_cinacalcet"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/bcp.13900> (open access, PMC6533487)

Chen et al. pooled cinacalcet plasma concentrations, serum intact parathyroid
hormone (iPTH) and corrected serum calcium (cCa) from eight Amgen studies in
adults and children with secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) on dialysis, plus
healthy adults. Cinacalcet PK is a two-compartment model with lagged first-order
absorption and allometric weight scaling on CL/F and the central volume. The
PK/PD model is semi-mechanistic (Chen 2019 Table 2 and Figure 1):

* Calcium-sensing-receptor (CaSR) occupancy by ionized calcium,
  `rho = x / (x + 1)` with `x = (0.45 * cCa / KD) * (1 + Ratio * Cp)`, where
  cinacalcet acts as a positive allosteric modulator (Ratio = alpha / Ki).
* Pseudo-steady-state iPTH, `iPTH = PTH0 * (rho / rho0)^lambda`, with
  `lambda < 0` so that higher occupancy suppresses PTH.
* Corrected-calcium turnover,
  `d cCa / dt = Kin,Ca * (iPTH / PTH0)^gamma - Kout,Ca * cCa`, with
  `Kin,Ca = Ca0 * Kout,Ca`.

Healthy volunteers and patients have separate PD parameter sets (Table 4); in
the packaged model the `DIS_HEALTHY` covariate selects the set.

# Population

The analysis used 648 subjects from eight studies (Chen 2019 Table 1): four
paediatric SHPT studies on dialysis (n = 84, age 28 days to 18 years), three
adult SHPT studies (n = 485, including the 403-subject phase 3 study 20000172)
and one healthy-adult study (n = 79). Doses were 1-300 mg orally, as single
doses, fixed once-daily regimens and titrated once-daily regimens. Children
contributed fewer than 15% of samples. The paper prints no table of baseline
demographics (weight, sex or race), and 34.7% of PK samples were below the
0.1 ng/mL limit of quantification.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Chen_2019_cinacalcet")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| PK structure (2-cmt, lag, first-order absorption and elimination) | n/a | Results paragraph 1; Figure 1 |
| `lka` | log(0.80) 1/h | Table 3 'Ka' (unit printed as L/h) |
| `lcl` | log(287.74) L/h | Table 3 'CL/F'; Abstract |
| `lvc` | log(4104.15) L | Table 3 'V2/F' |
| `lvp` | log(19824.20) L | Table 3 'V3/F' |
| `lq` | log(296.3) L/h | Table 3 'Q/F' |
| `ltlag` | log(0.36) h | Table 3 'Tlag' |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.75, 1 (fixed) | Results after Table 2; Discussion |
| Reference weight | 70 kg (assumed) | not printed; see Assumptions |
| `kd_ca` | 1.2 mM (fixed) | Table 2, Equation 1 |
| `f_ionized_ca` | 0.45 (fixed) | Table 2, Equation 1 |
| Occupancy with drug | n/a | Table 2, Equations 4-5 |
| Pseudo-steady-state iPTH | n/a | Table 2, Equation 2 |
| cCa turnover, `Kin = Ca0 * Kout` | n/a | Table 2, Equations 3 and 6 |
| `lrbase_pth_patient` / `_hv` | log(54.29) / log(2.38) pM | Table 4 'PTH0' |
| `lrbase_ca_patient` / `_hv` | log(2.45) / log(2.30) mM | Table 4 'Ca0' |
| `lratio_patient` / `_hv` | log(0.072) / log(0.02) | Table 4 'Ratio' |
| `lkout_ca_patient` / `_hv` | log(0.03) / log(0.01) 1/h | Table 4 'Kout,Ca' (unit printed as L/h) |
| `lgamma_pth_patient` / `_hv` | log(0.07) / log(1.80) | Table 4 'Power on PTH' |
| `lambda_ro_patient` / `_hv` | -3.30 / -10.03 | Table 4 'Power on RO' |
| IIV Ka, CL/F, V2/F, V3/F, Q/F, Tlag; corr(CL, V2) | 102, 76, 69, 86, 68, 34% CV; 0.85 | Table 3 |
| IIV PTH0, Ca0, Ratio, power on PTH, power on RO | 64, 6.6, 80.51, 112.51, 75.07% CV | Table 4 |
| PK residual, phase 3 / other studies | 72% / 50% CV | Table 3 |
| iPTH residual, patients / HV | 43% / 23% CV | Table 4 |
| cCa residual, patients / HV | 7% / 3.73% CV | Table 4 |

Variances are `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`. The residual errors are additive on the
log scale (Methods: 'additive error models after natural logarithmic
transformation'), encoded as `lnorm()` with `SD = sqrt(log(1 + CV^2))`.

# Typical-value checks

```{r typical-setup}
mod <- readModelDb("Chen_2019_cinacalcet")
ui <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)
ini_val <- setNames(ui$iniDf$est, ui$iniDf$name)
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(ui)

# Calcium turnover half-life. Chen 2019 Results: 'slow turnover of Ca with a
# half-life of 23.1 hours'.
t_half_ca <- log(2) / exp(ini_val[["lkout_ca_patient"]])
t_half_ca
stopifnot(abs(t_half_ca - 23.1) < 0.05)

# Distribution-phase half-life of a typical subject at a given weight,
# from the two-compartment micro-constants.
alpha_half_life <- function(wt) {
  cl <- exp(ini_val[["lcl"]]) * (wt / 70)^0.75
  vc <- exp(ini_val[["lvc"]]) * (wt / 70)
  q <- exp(ini_val[["lq"]])
  vp <- exp(ini_val[["lvp"]])
  k10 <- cl / vc
  k12 <- q / vc
  k21 <- q / vp
  s <- k10 + k12 + k21
  alpha <- (s + sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
  log(2) / alpha
}
tibble(WT = c(15, 25, 40, 70, 90)) |>
  mutate(`Distribution t1/2 (h)` = signif(alpha_half_life(WT), 3)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical distribution-phase half-life by body weight.")
```

The paper reports median distribution-phase half-lives of 4.27 h in adults and
2.29 h in children. The typical 70 kg adult gives
`r signif(alpha_half_life(70), 3)` h and a typical 25 kg child
`r signif(alpha_half_life(25), 3)` h; both are of the right size, and the
cohort medians below are compared directly.

The concentration unit of the allosteric ratio (see Assumptions and deviations)
is checked against Figure 3, panel II-A, where adults on the 30 mg starting dose
show a mean iPTH fall of roughly 20% over the first weeks.

```{r typical-30mg}
ev30 <- rxode2::et(amt = 30, ii = 24, addl = 27, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(c(0, 27 * 24 + 23.99), cmt = "ca") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(WT = 70, DIS_HEALTHY = 0L, STUDY_PHASE3 = 0L)
typ30 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev30, returnType = "data.frame")
pth_trough_chg <- 100 * (typ30$pth[2] / typ30$pth[1] - 1)
pth_trough_chg
# With the concentration in ng/mL the typical trough fall is about 21%; read
# in nmol/L (x 2.8) it would be about 43%, and in mmol/L about 0%.
stopifnot(pth_trough_chg > -30, pth_trough_chg < -12)
```

# Virtual cohorts

The paper does not print the weight distributions it simulated: adult weights
were 'sampled from demographics in cinacalcet clinical trials' and paediatric
age and weight were drawn jointly from NHANES. The cohorts below approximate
them. Adult weight is log-normal (median 75 kg, SD 0.2 on the log scale,
redrawn outside 40-150 kg). Paediatric weight is the CDC 50th-percentile weight
for an age drawn uniformly between 2 and 18 years, with log-normal scatter (SD
0.15), redrawn below 12.5 kg (the lightest band of the dosing tables).

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20190212)

draw_adult_wt <- function(n) {
  wt <- stats::rlnorm(n, log(75), 0.2)
  bad <- wt < 40 | wt > 150
  while (any(bad)) {
    wt[bad] <- stats::rlnorm(sum(bad), log(75), 0.2)
    bad <- wt < 40 | wt > 150
  }
  wt
}

# CDC 50th percentile weight-for-age, averaged across sexes.
growth <- tibble::tribble(
  ~age, ~wt,
  2, 12.2,
  3, 14.3,
  4, 16.3,
  5, 18.3,
  6, 20.6,
  7, 23.0,
  8, 25.6,
  10, 32.0,
  12, 40.5,
  14, 50.0,
  16, 58.0,
  18, 63.0
)
draw_ped <- function(n) {
  age <- stats::runif(n, 2, 18)
  wt <- stats::approx(growth$age, growth$wt, xout = age)$y *
    exp(stats::rnorm(n, 0, 0.15))
  bad <- wt < 12.5
  while (any(bad)) {
    age[bad] <- stats::runif(sum(bad), 2, 18)
    wt[bad] <- stats::approx(growth$age, growth$wt, xout = age[bad])$y *
      exp(stats::rnorm(sum(bad), 0, 0.15))
    bad <- wt < 12.5
  }
  tibble(AGE = age, WT = wt)
}
```

# Paediatric starting doses vs the adult 30 mg dose (Supporting Information S6-S7)

Chen 2019 simulated 4 weeks of once-daily dosing at the paediatric starting
doses of the SmPC dosing table (Supporting Information Table S2.1, based on dry
weight) and concluded that every paediatric starting dose gives a PK exposure
'less than or similar to' the adult 30 mg dose. Below, 150 virtual children
are assigned their weight-band starting dose and compared with 150 adults on
30 mg.

```{r startdose-cohort}
n_adult <- 150L
n_ped <- 150L
ped <- draw_ped(n_ped)
start_dose <- function(wt) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    wt < 12.5 ~ 1,
    wt < 25 ~ 2.5,
    wt < 50 ~ 5,
    wt < 75 ~ 10,
    TRUE ~ 15
  )
}
subjects <- bind_rows(
  tibble(id = seq_len(n_adult), WT = draw_adult_wt(n_adult), dose = 30, treatment = "Adult 30 mg"),
  tibble(id = n_adult + seq_len(n_ped), WT = ped$WT) |>
    mutate(
      dose = start_dose(WT),
      treatment = sprintf("Paediatric %s mg", dose)
    )
) |>
  mutate(DIS_HEALTHY = 0L, STUDY_PHASE3 = 0L)
count(subjects, treatment)

obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
  0:24, 216:240, 648:672, seq(0, 672, by = 24)
)))
doses <- subjects |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 27 * 24, by = 24)) |>
  mutate(evid = 1L, amt = dose, cmt = "depot")
obs <- subjects |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "ca")
events <- bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, WT, DIS_HEALTHY, STUDY_PHASE3, treatment)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events,
  keep = c("treatment", "WT"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
```

```{r startdose-figure, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
sim |>
  filter(time >= 648, time <= 672) |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time - 648, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after the day-28 dose (h)", y = "Cinacalcet (ng/mL)",
    title = "Steady-state cinacalcet by starting dose",
    caption = "Median and 90% prediction interval. Compare Supporting Information S6-S7 of Chen 2019."
  )
```

## PKNCA

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, treatment, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 216, 648),
  end = c(24, 240, 672),
  cmax = TRUE,
  tmax = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE),
  auclast = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  conc_obj, dose_obj,
  intervals = intervals,
  options = list(conc.blq = list(first = "keep", middle = "keep", last = "keep"))
))
nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result)

nca_tbl |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast"), start %in% c(0, 648)) |>
  mutate(
    interval = ifelse(start == 0, "Day 1", "Day 28"),
    param = paste(PPTESTCD, interval)
  ) |>
  group_by(treatment, param) |>
  summarise(median = signif(median(PPORRES), 3), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = param, values_from = median) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Group" = treatment,
    "Cmax day 1 (ng/mL)" = `cmax Day 1`,
    "AUC0-24 day 1 (ng*h/mL)" = `auclast Day 1`,
    "Cmax day 28 (ng/mL)" = `cmax Day 28`,
    "AUC0-24 day 28 (ng*h/mL)" = `auclast Day 28`
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median simulated NCA by starting-dose group.")
```

```{r startdose-check}
auc_ss <- nca_tbl |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast", start == 648) |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(med = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")
adult_auc <- auc_ss$med[auc_ss$treatment == "Adult 30 mg"]
ped_auc <- auc_ss$med[auc_ss$treatment != "Adult 30 mg"]
# 'Less than or similar to' the adult 30 mg exposure. The largest paediatric
# starting dose (15 mg at >= 75 kg) is half the adult dose at a similar weight.
stopifnot(all(ped_auc < 0.8 * adult_auc))
```

Every paediatric starting-dose group has a median steady-state AUC below the
adult 30 mg median (`r signif(adult_auc, 3)` ng*h/mL), as the paper concludes.
The paper reports no NCA table, so there is nothing numeric to place beside
these values in a comparison table.

## Accumulation and distribution half-life

Chen 2019 reports a median accumulation ratio on day 10 of 1.69 in adults and
1.93 across paediatric ages, and median distribution-phase half-lives of 4.27 h
(adults) and 2.29 h (children).

```{r accumulation}
acc <- nca_tbl |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast", start %in% c(0, 216)) |>
  select(id, treatment, start, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = start, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  mutate(rac = `216` / `0`, adult = treatment == "Adult 30 mg")

hl <- sim |>
  distinct(id, treatment, kel, k12, k21) |>
  mutate(
    s = kel + k12 + k21,
    t_half_alpha = log(2) / ((s + sqrt(s^2 - 4 * kel * k21)) / 2),
    adult = treatment == "Adult 30 mg"
  )

acc_sum <- acc |>
  group_by(adult) |>
  summarise(rac = median(rac), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(
    hl |> group_by(adult) |> summarise(t_half = median(t_half_alpha), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "adult"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Group = ifelse(adult, "Adults", "Children"),
    `Published Rac day 10` = ifelse(adult, 1.69, 1.93),
    `Published t1/2 alpha (h)` = ifelse(adult, 4.27, 2.29)
  )
acc_sum |>
  transmute(
    Group,
    `Simulated Rac day 10` = signif(rac, 3),
    `Published Rac day 10`,
    `Simulated t1/2 alpha (h)` = signif(t_half, 3),
    `Published t1/2 alpha (h)`
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median accumulation ratio (AUC0-24 day 10 / day 1) and distribution half-life.")
```

# Titrated-dose trial simulations (Figure 3, Table 5)

Chen 2019 simulated 24 weeks of titrated once-daily dosing in adults (the Study
20000172 algorithm, Supporting Information S3) and in children (the Study
20070208 algorithm with weekly calcium monitoring, Supporting Information S4-S5).
The helper below steps the trial forward one week at a time. Individual random
effects are drawn once per subject and held fixed, each week's dose is chosen
from the observed (residual-error-perturbed) trough iPTH and cCa, and the
deterministic model is re-solved over the whole dose history.

```{r titration-helpers}
omega <- ui$omega
pd_sd <- c(
  pth = ini_val[["expSd_pth_patient"]],
  ca = ini_val[["expSd_ca_patient"]]
)

draw_eta <- function(n) {
  eta <- rxode2::rxRmvn(n, rep(0, nrow(omega)), omega)
  colnames(eta) <- rownames(omega)
  as.data.frame(eta)
}

# Trough predictions (just before the next dose) at the end of weeks 0..max(week)
# for a list of per-subject daily dose vectors (one value per day).
solve_troughs <- function(cohort, eta, daily_dose, n_week) {
  n_day <- 7 * n_week
  dose_rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(cohort)), function(i) {
    d <- daily_dose[[i]][seq_len(n_day)]
    data.frame(id = cohort$id[i], time = 24 * (seq_len(n_day) - 1), amt = d)
  }))
  dose_rows <- dose_rows[dose_rows$amt > 0, ]
  dose_rows$evid <- 1L
  dose_rows$cmt <- "depot"
  obs_rows <- tidyr::crossing(id = cohort$id, week = 0:n_week) |>
    mutate(time = pmax(168 * week - 0.01, 0), evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "ca") |>
    select(-week)
  ev <- bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    left_join(cohort |> select(id, WT, DIS_HEALTHY, STUDY_PHASE3), by = "id") |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod_typ,
    events = ev,
    params = cbind(id = cohort$id, eta),
    returnType = "data.frame"
  )
  out |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    mutate(week = round((time + 0.01) / 168)) |>
    select(id, week, Cc, pth, ca)
}
```

```{r titration-adult}
# Study 20000172 (Supporting Information S3): start 30 mg; at weeks 3, 6, 9
# and 12 step up 30 -> 60 -> 90 -> 120 -> 180 mg unless the mean of the iPTH
# values from the two preceding weeks is <= 200 pg/mL (21.2 pmol/L) or serum
# calcium is < 7.8 mg/dL (1.95 mmol/L).
run_adult_trial <- function(n, n_week = 26) {
  cohort <- tibble(id = seq_len(n), WT = draw_adult_wt(n), DIS_HEALTHY = 0L, STUDY_PHASE3 = 1L)
  eta <- draw_eta(n)
  ladder <- c(30, 60, 90, 120, 180)
  level <- rep(1L, n)
  daily <- lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) rep(30, 7 * n_week))
  eps_pth <- matrix(stats::rnorm(n * (n_week + 2), 0, pd_sd[["pth"]]), n)
  eps_ca <- matrix(stats::rnorm(n * (n_week + 2), 0, pd_sd[["ca"]]), n)
  for (w in c(3, 6, 9, 12)) {
    tr <- solve_troughs(cohort, eta, daily, w) |> arrange(id, week)
    pth_obs <- matrix(tr$pth, n, byrow = TRUE) * exp(eps_pth[, 1:(w + 1)])
    ca_obs <- matrix(tr$ca, n, byrow = TRUE) * exp(eps_ca[, 1:(w + 1)])
    mean_pth <- rowMeans(pth_obs[, c(w, w + 1), drop = FALSE])
    up <- mean_pth > 21.2 & ca_obs[, w + 1] >= 1.95 & level < length(ladder)
    level[up] <- level[up] + 1L
    for (i in which(up)) daily[[i]][(7 * w + 1):(7 * n_week)] <- ladder[level[i]]
  }
  tr <- solve_troughs(cohort, eta, daily, n_week) |> arrange(id, week)
  tr$pth_obs <- tr$pth * exp(as.vector(t(eps_pth[, 1:(n_week + 1)])))
  tr$ca_obs <- tr$ca * exp(as.vector(t(eps_ca[, 1:(n_week + 1)])))
  base_obs <- tibble(id = cohort$id, pth_base_obs = tr$pth[tr$week == 0] * exp(eps_pth[, n_week + 2]))
  tr$dose <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(tr)), function(j) {
    daily[[tr$id[j]]][min(7 * tr$week[j] + 1, 7 * n_week)]
  }, numeric(1))
  tr |> left_join(base_obs, by = "id")
}

summarise_trial <- function(tr) {
  tr |>
    group_by(id) |>
    mutate(pth0 = pth[week == 0], ca0 = ca[week == 0]) |>
    ungroup() |>
    group_by(week) |>
    summarise(
      pth_chg = mean(100 * (pth / pth0 - 1)),
      pth_resp = 100 * mean(pth_obs <= 0.7 * pth_base_obs),
      ca_chg = mean(100 * (ca / ca0 - 1)),
      ca_low = 100 * mean(ca_obs <= 2.1),
      mean_dose = mean(dose),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

adult_trial <- run_adult_trial(200)
adult_sum <- summarise_trial(adult_trial)
```

```{r titration-ped}
# Study 20070208 (Supporting Information S4, Table S4.1): weight-band dose
# ladders; step up at weeks 4, 8, ..., 24 if iPTH >= 300 pg/mL (31.8 pmol/L)
# and cCa >= 8.4 mg/dL (2.1 mmol/L); step down if 100 <= iPTH < 150 pg/mL
# (10.6-15.9 pmol/L) or 8.0 <= cCa < 8.4 mg/dL (2.0-2.1 mmol/L); withhold if
# iPTH < 100 pg/mL or cCa < 8.0 mg/dL, restarting one level lower once iPTH
# > 150 pg/mL and cCa >= 8.4 mg/dL. Calcium and iPTH are checked weekly.
ped_ladder <- function(wt) {
  if (wt <= 14) return(c(2.5, 5, 10, 15, 30, 30, 30))
  if (wt <= 21) return(c(2.5, 5, 10, 15, 30, 60, 60))
  if (wt <= 25) return(c(2.5, 5, 10, 15, 30, 60, 90))
  if (wt <= 28) return(c(5, 10, 15, 30, 60, 90, 90))
  if (wt <= 49) return(c(5, 10, 15, 30, 60, 90, 120))
  if (wt < 75) return(c(10, 15, 30, 60, 90, 120, 180))
  c(15, 30, 60, 90, 120, 180, 180)
}

run_ped_trial <- function(n, n_week = 26) {
  # Screening (Supporting Information S5): iPTH >= 350 pg/mL (37.1 pmol/L)
  # and cCa >= 8.8 mg/dL (2.2 mmol/L) in at least one of three simulated
  # screening observations.
  cohort <- tibble(id = integer(0))
  eta <- NULL
  while (nrow(cohort) < n) {
    cand <- draw_ped(4 * n) |> mutate(DIS_HEALTHY = 0L, STUDY_PHASE3 = 0L)
    e <- draw_eta(4 * n)
    pth0 <- exp(ini_val[["lrbase_pth_patient"]] + e$etalrbase_pth)
    ca0 <- exp(ini_val[["lrbase_ca_patient"]] + e$etalrbase_ca)
    ok <- vapply(seq_len(4 * n), function(i) {
      any(pth0[i] * exp(stats::rnorm(3, 0, pd_sd[["pth"]])) >= 37.1 &
        ca0[i] * exp(stats::rnorm(3, 0, pd_sd[["ca"]])) >= 2.2)
    }, logical(1))
    cohort <- bind_rows(cohort, cand[ok, ])
    eta <- rbind(eta, e[ok, ])
  }
  cohort <- cohort[seq_len(n), ] |> mutate(id = seq_len(n))
  eta <- eta[seq_len(n), ]
  ladders <- lapply(cohort$WT, ped_ladder)
  level <- rep(1L, n)
  held <- rep(FALSE, n)
  daily <- lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) rep(ladders[[i]][1], 7 * n_week))
  eps_pth <- matrix(stats::rnorm(n * (n_week + 2), 0, pd_sd[["pth"]]), n)
  eps_ca <- matrix(stats::rnorm(n * (n_week + 2), 0, pd_sd[["ca"]]), n)
  for (w in 1:(n_week - 1)) {
    tr <- solve_troughs(cohort, eta, daily, w) |> filter(week == w) |> arrange(id)
    pth_obs <- tr$pth * exp(eps_pth[, w + 1])
    ca_obs <- tr$ca * exp(eps_ca[, w + 1])
    for (i in seq_len(n)) {
      if (held[i]) {
        if (pth_obs[i] > 15.9 && ca_obs[i] >= 2.1) {
          held[i] <- FALSE
          level[i] <- max(1L, level[i] - 1L)
        }
      } else if (ca_obs[i] < 2.0 || pth_obs[i] < 10.6) {
        held[i] <- TRUE
      } else if (pth_obs[i] < 15.9 || ca_obs[i] < 2.1) {
        level[i] <- max(1L, level[i] - 1L)
      } else if (w %% 4 == 0 && w <= 24 && pth_obs[i] >= 31.8 && level[i] < 7L) {
        level[i] <- level[i] + 1L
      }
      daily[[i]][(7 * w + 1):(7 * n_week)] <- if (held[i]) 0 else ladders[[i]][level[i]]
    }
  }
  tr <- solve_troughs(cohort, eta, daily, n_week) |> arrange(id, week)
  tr$pth_obs <- tr$pth * exp(as.vector(t(eps_pth[, 1:(n_week + 1)])))
  tr$ca_obs <- tr$ca * exp(as.vector(t(eps_ca[, 1:(n_week + 1)])))
  base_obs <- tibble(id = cohort$id, pth_base_obs = tr$pth[tr$week == 0] * exp(eps_pth[, n_week + 2]))
  tr$dose <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(tr)), function(j) {
    daily[[tr$id[j]]][min(7 * tr$week[j] + 1, 7 * n_week)]
  }, numeric(1))
  tr |> left_join(base_obs, by = "id")
}

ped_trial <- run_ped_trial(200)
ped_sum <- summarise_trial(ped_trial)
```


```{r titration-check}
a24 <- wk24[wk24$population == "Adults", ]
p24 <- wk24[wk24$population == "Children", ]
stopifnot(
  # Adults: mean iPTH and cCa change at week 24 (published -42.1% and -7.4%).
  # The tolerance covers a single 200-subject trial and the unpublished
  # adult weight distribution; a transcription error in PTH0, Ca0, Kout or a
  # power exponent moves these by more.
  abs(a24$pth_chg - (-42.1)) < 15,
  abs(a24$ca_chg - (-7.4)) < 3,
  # Children respond less than adults (Results, Figure 3, Table 5).
  p24$pth_chg > a24$pth_chg,
  p24$ca_chg > a24$ca_chg
)
```

Before the first dose (week 0), the simulated fraction of subjects whose
observed iPTH is already 30% below their observed baseline is
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", adult_sum$pth_resp[adult_sum$week == 0])` (adults) and
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", ped_sum$pth_resp[ped_sum$week == 0])` (children), and the
fraction with observed cCa <= 8.4 mg/dL is
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", adult_sum$ca_low[adult_sum$week == 0])` and
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", ped_sum$ca_low[ped_sum$week == 0])`. Figure 3 starts at
about 22% and about 5% rather than at zero, so the published fractions include
residual error, as the simulation here does. Two independent iPTH draws with
the patient residual SD give a pre-dose 'responder' fraction of
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * pnorm(log(0.7) / (sqrt(2) * pd_sd[["pth"]])))`.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Reference weight for allometry.** Chen 2019 states that CL/F and the
  central V/F carry fixed allometric exponents (0.75 and 1) but does not print
  the reference weight. The maintainers assumed 70 kg. With that choice the
  typical distribution half-life is close to the published medians (see the
  typical-value checks), but those medians depend on the unpublished weight
  distributions and cannot pin the reference weight. Q/F and V3/F are not
  weight-scaled (Discussion: allometry applied to 'clearance and the apparent
  volume of distribution for the central compartment').
* **Concentration unit in the occupancy term.** Table 4 prints the allosteric
  ratio in 'L mM-1' and the Results text in 'mM-1'. A plasma cinacalcet
  concentration in mmol/L (about 1e-5 mM at clinical doses) would make the drug
  effect vanish. With the concentration in ng/mL, the model reproduces the
  adult iPTH and cCa responses of Figure 3 and Table 5; with the concentration
  in nmol/L it overshoots them about two-fold (a typical adult on 30 mg falls
  42% in trough iPTH rather than the roughly 20% of Figure 3, panel II-A). The
  packaged model therefore multiplies `ratio` by `Cc` in ng/mL.
* **Unit typos.** Table 3 prints Ka in 'L h-1' and Table 4 prints Kout,Ca in
  'L h-1'; both are first-order rate constants in 1/h (the Ca half-life of
  23.1 h equals log(2) / 0.03 h).
* **Parameter naming in the text.** The Results text calls the power on the
  change of receptor occupancy 'gamma' (-3.3), while Table 2 calls it lambda
  (Equation 2) and uses gamma for the power on the iPTH change (Equation 3).
  The packaged model follows Tables 2 and 4: `lambda_ro` = -3.30 (power on RO),
  `gamma_pth` = 0.07 (power on PTH). The text quotes PD IIV of '78-133% CV'
  while Table 4 prints 64-112.51%; the table values are used.
* **IIV on a negative parameter.** The power on receptor occupancy is negative;
  its exponential IIV (Table 2 Equation 7) is applied as
  `lambda_ro * exp(eta)`, keeping the sign.
* **Residual error scale.** Tables 3 and 4 give the log-scale additive residual
  errors as '% CV'. They are converted with `SD = sqrt(log(1 + CV^2))`, the
  same conversion as the IIV. Reading them directly as SDs (0.50, 0.72, 0.43,
  0.07, 0.23, 0.0373) differs by at most 0.07 on the log scale. The week-0
  fractions in Figure 3 (about 22% of subjects already 'responding' and about
  5% with cCa <= 8.4 mg/dL before treatment) are consistent with the published
  simulations including residual error, which the trial simulation above does.
* **Shared IIV across strata.** Table 4 prints one IIV per PD parameter; it is
  applied to both the patient and the healthy-volunteer parameter sets.
  `Kout,Ca` has no IIV.
* **Healthy-volunteer and phase 3 strata.** `DIS_HEALTHY = 1` selects the
  healthy-volunteer PD parameters and residual errors; `STUDY_PHASE3 = 1`
  selects the phase 3 PK residual error. Both default to the patient /
  non-phase-3 case in the simulations above unless stated.
* **Virtual cohorts.** Adult weights and paediatric age-weight pairs are
  assumptions (see Virtual cohorts); the paper sampled NHANES for children and
  unspecified trial demographics for adults. Children are restricted to 2-18
  years and at least 12.5 kg, the range covered by the Study 20070208 dose
  table; the paper's paediatric simulations also included younger children.
* **Titration algorithms.** The adult algorithm decides on the trough iPTH of
  the two preceding weekly visits; the paediatric algorithm checks trough iPTH
  and cCa weekly (the paper's simulation used weekly cCa monitoring) and
  applies the Study 20070208 step-up, step-down and withhold rules. Adverse-event
  criteria cannot be simulated and are omitted. No adult inclusion criteria are
  printed, so all simulated adults are enrolled.
* **Errata.** No correction notice for this article was found on EuropePMC as
  of 2026-11-25.
